result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): A makes a clear call for a one-time 50–100 page credit plus a free sandbox. Its arithmetic is correct, it ties the cost to the tight runway, and it says to track free-to-paid conversion without inventing a benchmark figure. B also commits to one option and sizes exposure well, but it relies on invented conversion rates (2%, 1%) and gets a revenue figure wrong: 2% of 2,000 × $10 is $400, not $200. It also handles repeat signups less directly. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Answer B gives a clear, cheap direction: a one-time 50–100 page credit plus a free sandbox, with correct cost math. It names what to track without inventing conversion rates and covers throwaway accounts and a spend ceiling. Answer A is decisive and its main arithmetic is right, but it leans on assumed conversion rates of 1–2% for its break-even logic, which it states unclearly, and it recommends a 50-page cap after showing that a $500 budget only funds about 12 pages.
